name: Risk Suite
description: Tests whether a model can identify unintended consequences, fragility, and perverse incentives.

tasks.billText: Section 101. The Department of Agriculture shall reimburse agricultural producers for 100 percent of reported crop and livestock losses. Reimbursements under this section are not subject to payment caps, audit requirements, or minimum loss-prevention standards.
tasks.rationale: Full uncapped reimbursement without audits or prevention standards invites fraud, moral hazard, and uncontrolled exposure.

tasks.billText: Section 202. For a period of 10 years, the lawful rent for any multifamily residential unit shall not exceed the rent charged for that unit on the effective date of this Act. No hardship exemption, maintenance adjustment, or new-construction exception shall apply under this section.
tasks.rationale: The rigid rent freeze creates predictable downstream risks to maintenance, supply, and investment without safety valves.

tasks.billText: Section 303. The Housing Stability Department shall administer a two-year pilot program for emergency rental assistance. Program expenditures are limited to the amounts appropriated for the pilot, applicant verification and fraud screening are required, the department shall submit a program evaluation after 18 months, and the pilot shall terminate on schedule unless reauthorized by the legislature.
tasks.rationale: The program is bounded, monitored, and subject to fraud controls, evaluation, and sunset.

tasks.billText: Section 404. The state shall guarantee 95 percent of principal on all loans issued by participating lenders to newly formed technology firms. Lenders may rely on borrower self-certification of projected revenue, and no portfolio concentration limits or clawback provisions shall apply to repeated defaults.
tasks.rationale: The guarantee structure invites adverse selection and weak underwriting by socializing downside risk without strong lender discipline or concentration controls.

tasks.billText: Section 405. The Department of Forestry shall create a three-year pilot grant for home-hardening in wildfire-prone areas. Grants are limited by annual appropriations, homeowners must complete approved mitigation measures before reimbursement, the department shall publish risk-reduction criteria, and the pilot shall pause automatically if post-award inspections show noncompliance above 10 percent in any grant cycle.
tasks.rationale: The pilot includes appropriation limits, verified mitigation requirements, published criteria, and a built-in circuit breaker if the program begins to drift.
